band_change_evidence_test.explanation: The test fails on the tier requirement. Four independent sources support the assessment — Interesting Engineering, The Robot Report, Climate Investment and SAP News — which satisfies the two-source part. But none reaches tier 4. AnyBotics publishes no institutional data, no responsibility report and no audited disclosure, and the ANYmal X Ex certificate itself could not be obtained. The strongest available evidence is tier-3 trade reporting. This failure is itself the finding: the entity cannot be verified at tier 4 in either direction, which is precisely why a placeholder asserting tier-4-level practice was indefensible.

key_evidence: Why it matters: AnyBotics has the clearest measurable worker-safety benefit in the cluster, and almost no institutional disclosure. Those two facts pull its score in opposite directions.

One ANYmal robot completed more than 33,000 inspections at Vigier Ciment’s 150-year-old Swiss cement plant since early 2025, working nights across 450 checkpoints in narrow stairways, dust and heat — work that previously exposed people to those conditions.

ANYmal X is described as the world’s first Ex-certified legged robot, meaning an independent body certified it for atmospheres containing flammable gas, vapour or dust. That is the only third-party product certification found in this cluster.

AnyBotics publishes no responsibility report, no workforce data, no failure disclosure and no reparative-action record. Its entire Accountability dimension scores 2.0 on absence of disclosure, not on any located misconduct.
No adverse conduct of any kind was located for AnyBotics — no lawsuits, no safety incidents, no labour findings.

notes: FLAG FOR REVIEW — SEED CORRECTION, NOT A CONDUCT DOWNGRADE. The published 60.9 is a never-assessed uniform placeholder shared byte-for-byte with nine other robotics labs. AnyBotics has never been individually assessed. NO adverse evidence of any kind was located. The entire 24.6-point gap measures missing disclosure against a placeholder, exactly as in the Cerebras Systems case. Twenty-four of forty subdimensions score at the low anchor for absence of disclosure. The band-change evidence test FAILS: no source at tier 4 or above was obtainable for this entity, because it publishes no institutional data. A coordinator should treat the band change as provisional pending either company disclosure or an obtained copy of the ANYmal X Ex certificate.
